# What is the actual effect of noslip_iterations in the original post when grasp normal force is much greater than gravity demand?

> **Current answer:** In the 45 g capsule minimum reproduction in MuJoCo 3.8.1, the default elliptic/impratio=10 results in a steady-state downward speed of ~155 µm/s; setting noslip_iterations=10 reduces this to ~1.41 µm/s, a ~110-fold improvement. The maintainer confirms this regularization friction creep is the expected behavior. This parameter is only quantified in this MRE and cannot be used to claim other grasp tasks are completely static.

## Key terms

- Regularization friction (正则化摩擦)
- Noslip iterations (防滑迭代)
- Tangential creep (切向爬移)

## Problem and symptoms

- Why does an object continue to slowly descend when the normal force is much greater than gravity demand?
- Default elliptic/impratio=10 results in ~155 µm/s steady-state creep; pyramidal is faster when impratio=1.

## Environment

- MuJoCo 3.8.1; Python 3.12; Linux x86_64 CPU; 45 g capsule; µ=0.7; timestep=0.002.

## Priority diagnostics

- Measure downward speed, normal force, and rotation, to exclude rolling and z-motion of gripper.
- Separately scan cone, impratio, condim, solref, and noslip_iterations.

## Possible causes

- The post attributes the phenomenon to regularization friction in the vicinity of the origin—slip speed mapping; maintainer confirms behavior is expected.

## Attempts

- Increase impratio.
- Set noslip_iterations=10.
- Change cone, condim, and solref.

## Result

- noslip_iterations=10 reduces creep speed by ~110-fold in this MRE; maintainer confirms behavior is expected, but no general parameter recommendation is given.
